title: [TASK] Pin the gate steps of the non-RTL required contexts: step-level if / continue-on-error / || true on docs-check's ci_events step, wire-accountability's gate step, docs-check-no-git's single step and elaborate's scope step pass --check

milestone.title: First Milan 1x1 8 channels simulation
milestone.description: Ensure a correct quality, tracing and CI/CD

body:
## Objective / problem

PR #293 (#261) holds the JOB carrying each non-RTL required context
(`docs-check`, `wire-accountability`, `docs-check-no-git`, `elaborate`) to
the no-`needs`/`if`/`continue-on-error`/`defaults` rule and requires the
job of that id to carry the name. The gate STEPS inside those jobs are still
unpinned, so the same levers one level down retire each gate with every
required context green.

## Evidence / motivation

Measured by the [R3] round on PR #293 at `2bd7e57f` (each returns
`ci_events: OK`, rc 0):

- a step-level `if: false`, `continue-on-error: true`, or `--check || true`
  on `docs-check`'s "CI event and SHA contract gate" step
  (`.github/workflows/docs.yml` ~:178) — `check_docs` holds that step by a
  substring recogniser (`"scripts/ci_events.py --check" in text`), which
  `--check || true` satisfies — while the neighbouring act_ci step IS
  key-pinned and refuses `if`;
- the same three levers on the gate step (third of three) of
  `wire-accountability` (~:258) and on the single step of
  `docs-check-no-git` (~:270);
- `if: false` on `elaborate`'s scope step (`elaborate.yml` ~:67), the scope
  script rewritten to publish `rtl=false`, or its `ci_scope.py --selftest`
  line removed: every gate step of `elaborate` is guarded by
  `steps.scope.outputs.rtl == 'true'` and the guard is pinned, but the step
  that publishes the output is not — the RTL gate's decide step is
  canonicalised for exactly this reason (#209).
- PRESENCE, not only shape ([R3] round 2 on PR #293 at `74056aa3`): the
  id rule PR #293 adds requires the job of id `wire-accountability` /
  `docs-check-no-git` to carry the name, but nothing pins what that job
  contains, so the real job's id renamed to `wire-accountability-real` (no
  `name:`) beside a stub `wire-accountability: {runs-on, steps: [run: true]}`
  — or the same through an appended duplicate `X:` mapping, PyYAML
  last-wins — returns `ci_events: OK (237 contract item(s))`. For
  `docs-check` and `elaborate` the builder contract refuses the stub (no
  checkout, no builder call); the two non-builder carriers have no such
  content check.

Expected: those steps are pinned the way the builder and gate steps already
are — exact key set, normalised script equal to a canonical form — each
refusal naming the step, with reason-pinned arms that fail when the checker
is stubbed.

## Authoritative references

- #261, PR #293 ([R3] findings MINOR Robustness ×2)
- `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` "Exhaustive validation" items 1–2 (how a
  step is pinned), 7 (the decide step), 11 (the job-level rule)
- `scripts/ci_events.py`: `pinned_step_keys`, `check_decide_step`,
  `check_docs`, `check_builder_dependencies`, `check_required_context_carriers`
- `scripts/ci_scope.py`

## Context entry points

Read first:
- `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md#exhaustive-validation`
- `scripts/ci_events.py` (the functions above and the `_mutations` arm list)
- `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, `.github/workflows/elaborate.yml`

## Scope

In scope:
- Pin the four steps named above (keys and normalised script), refusing
  `if`, `shell`, `continue-on-error`, `working-directory`, and a script
  that is not the canonical one; hold `elaborate`'s scope step as the
  decide step is held, including that `ci_scope.py --selftest` runs before
  the answer is read.
- Require each gate step to be PRESENT exactly once in the id-named job,
  so a job body replaced wholesale, a removed gate step, or a duplicate
  `X:` mapping is refused naming the job.
- Pin each of the four carriers' STEP LISTS the way item 4 pins the gate's
  (count, order, recognised steps; no `run:` or `uses:` step beyond the
  pinned ones) — [R4] round 6 on PR #293: a `run:` step inserted before the
  gates of `docs-check` or `docs-check-no-git` writing `BASH_ENV=…` to
  `$GITHUB_ENV`, one in `wire-accountability` prepending `$GITHUB_PATH`,
  or an inserted `uses:` of any third-party action, sets the inherited
  environment at RUN TIME for every later step, which PR #293's declared
  allowlist (policy item 12) cannot see; the same insertion in
  `full-ci-gate` is refused by its sequence pin.
- One arm per lever per step, reason-pinned; the vacuity control must fail
  them all.
- State the pinned steps on the policy page (item 11) and drop the "not yet
  pinned" caveat.

Out of scope:
- Changing what the gates do or which contexts are required.
- The RTL workflows (already held).

## Executor

Unassigned

## Independent reviewer

Unassigned

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each of the four steps refuses a step-level `if`, `continue-on-error`,
      `shell`, `working-directory` and a non-canonical script, naming the step.
- [ ] `elaborate`'s scope step refuses `if: false`, a script that publishes
      a literal `rtl`, and a dropped `ci_scope.py --selftest`.
- [ ] Each gate step is present exactly once in the job of the required
      name: the gate step removed, the job body replaced by `run: true`
      (with the real job's id renamed away), and an appended duplicate
      `X:` mapping are each refused naming the job, with arms.
- [ ] EVERY job's step list in the four workflow files is pinned the way
      `full-ci-gate`'s is (count, order, recognised steps) — the ten jobs
      without a sequence pin today, the RTL workers and aggregates included
      ([R3] round 9 on PR #293): an inserted step of ANY content is refused
      naming the job and the position, with arms, including one that
      reaches the runner's environment file without spelling its name (the
      `_runner_file_commands` glob, an indirect expansion, a checked-in
      script) and one under a recorded writer's name. PR #293's allowlists
      (declared `env`, key sets, token-bearing environment-file writes bound
      by script, recorded actions, checkout `with`) hold everything short of
      that; this row is what closes the class.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/ci_events.py --selftest` carries the arms and PASSes;
      `--check` is green on the pristine tree.
- [ ] `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md` item 11 states the steps as pinned;
      `docs_check`, `gen_toc --check`, `check_doc_paths` stay green.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --check
python3 scripts/ci_events.py --selftest
# by hand: each lever above on a copy of the workflow file, --check must exit 1 naming the step
```

Expected result: pristine tree green; every lever refused and named; every new arm caught and vacuity-controlled.

## Dependencies / lane conflicts

Depends on:
- PR #293 (the job-level rule and `check_required_context_carriers`)

May conflict with:
- concurrent edits to `scripts/ci_events.py`, `docs.yml`, `elaborate.yml`, `docs/testing/CI_WORKFLOWS.md`

## Open design/specification decision?

No — scope is settled and may become Ready

## Decision details (if applicable)

None.
